# Verified Functions Patterns

Illustrative fragments below assume imports in the project's `GlobalUsing.cs`. Replace `ImportService`, `ProductReadService` and `ProductFunctions` with actual application/local types; these are not framework classes.

## Startup

```csharp
var builder = FunctionsApplication.CreateBuilder(args);
builder.ConfigureFunctionsWebApplication();
builder.AddHostSettings();
builder.Services.AddExecutionContext();
builder.Services.AddMvc();
builder.Services.AddMvcWebApi((_, webApi) => webApi.ConvertUnhandledExceptionsToProblemDetails = true);
builder.Services.AddScoped<ImportService>();
builder.UseCoreExExecutionContext();
builder.Build().Run();
```

Only HTTP capabilities need ASP.NET integration/MVC registrations. The empty template and non-HTTP-only apps can use `FunctionsApplication.CreateBuilder` and CoreEx context middleware without these HTTP calls. `AddHostSettings()` reads the generated worker configuration; it is not binding configuration.

## HTTP delegation

```csharp
public sealed class ProductFunctions(CoreEx.AspNetCore.Mvc.WebApi webApi, ProductReadService service)
{
    [Function(nameof(GetProduct))]
    public Task<IActionResult> GetProduct([HttpTrigger(AuthorizationLevel.Function, "get", Route = "products/{id}")] HttpRequest request, string id, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
        => webApi.GetAsync(request, (_, ct) => service.GetAsync(id, ct), cancellationToken: cancellationToken);
}
```

Add XML documentation to real types/members per project conventions. Function-key authorization does not establish a user/tenant identity; configure those policies explicitly. Keep business failures within WebApi's chosen boundary and let failures outside it propagate.

## Idempotent HTTP operation

```csharp
return await webApi.FunctionWithIdempotencyAsync(request,
    ct => webApi.PostAsync<ImportRequest, ImportResponse>(request, (operation, token) => service.ImportAsync(operation.Value, token), cancellationToken: ct),
    isRequired: true, cancellationToken: cancellationToken).ConfigureAwait(false);
```

The configured provider/cache must already be registered. The helper eagerly renders and returns `EmptyResult`; never separately execute the returned result to recover a body for tests. Replay is a best-effort retry safeguard, not exactly-once execution.

## Explicit subscriber settlement

```csharp
private const string QueueName = "%ImportQueue%";

[Function(nameof(ImportMessage))]
public Task ImportMessage([ServiceBusTrigger(QueueName, Connection = "ServiceBus", AutoCompleteMessages = false)] ServiceBusReceivedMessage message, ServiceBusMessageActions actions, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
    => subscriber.FunctionReceiveAsync(message, actions, QueueName, cancellationToken: cancellationToken);
```

Here `subscriber` is an injected `ServiceBusSubscribedSubscriber` or a typed `ServiceBusSubscriberBase<T>` implementation. For a topic, share topic/subscription constants and pass the matching `topic/Subscriptions/subscription` expression to the bridge. Do not pass an unrelated label or add a competing receiver.

## Invocation tests

```csharp
using var test = FunctionTester.Create<ProductFunctions>();
var request = test.CreateHttpRequest(HttpMethod.Get, "products/example");
test.HttpTrigger<ProductFunctions>()
    .Run(f => f.GetProduct(request, "example", CancellationToken.None))
    .ToHttpResponseMessageAssertor(request)
    .AssertOK()
    .AssertValue(expectedProduct);
```

The `using var` above is resource disposal, not a namespace import. For an already-rendered idempotency response, set `request.HttpContext.Response.Body` to a caller-owned readable/seekable `MemoryStream`, invoke and use `.SnapshotHttpResponse(request.HttpContext.Response)`. Dispose the buffer after assertions.

```csharp
test.Trigger<ImportFunctions>()
    .Run(f => f.ImportBlob(blobClient, cancellationToken))
    .AssertSuccess();
```

Assertions must cover observable effects/delegation, not just `AssertSuccess`. For failures use `.AssertException<TException>()`; settlement tests can supply a recording `ServiceBusMessageActions` implementation. A direct invocation does not run binding conversion or enforce authorization.

## Native Blob and Timer

```csharp
[Function(nameof(ImportBlob))]
public Task ImportBlob([BlobTrigger("imports/{name}", Connection = "ImportStorage", Source = BlobTriggerSource.EventGrid)] BlobClient blob, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
    => service.ProcessAsync(blob, cancellationToken);

[Function(nameof(Scheduled))]
public Task Scheduled([TimerTrigger("%ImportSchedule%")] TimerInfo timer, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
    => service.ProcessScheduledAsync(cancellationToken);
```

These are separate illustrative entry points; do not generate both unless requested. The binding extensions own retries/poison behavior. Thread cancellation through SDK reads/writes; deterministic output naming alone does not make all downstream side effects exactly-once.
